newsitem.title: UK: Reliance Industries says plans no more bonds in 97.
newsitem.headline: Reliance Industries says plans no more bonds in 97.

text.p: India's largest private sector company, Reliance Industries Ltd, has no plans to tap the international bond markets again this year after launching a sterling Eurobond on Tuesday, an official said.
"One of the basic objectives of tapping sterling was to diversify our investor base," Mathew Panikar, managing director at Reliance Europe Ltd told Reuters.
"We achieved this and plan to diversify to other major global bond markets. (But) it is unlikely we will go to the international bond markets this year," he said.
Earlier, analysts in Bombay said Reliance was looking into launching bonds in marks and yen.
Panikar said Reliance Industries might tap these sectors in 1998, "provided there is appetite and we get attractive transaction costs".
Reliance Industries's business consists of textiles, polyester fibres, polymers and petrochemicals. It has also entered new areas such as energy and oil and gas.
Reliance is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BB+ by Standard & Poor's.
On Tuesday it issued a debut sterling bond. The 150 million stg 10-year transaction was priced to yield 165 basis points over gilts.
In the last two years, Reliance has raised about $800 million in the U.S. bond markets.
